To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dynamic material flow analysis of ENMs in Europe predicts accumulation of ENMs over time and regional differences in ENM flows and release concentrations.
dynamic material flows of ENMs in Europe are dominated by accumulation in stocks (in use and waste) and that environmental release concentrations vary between different regions.

the dynamic probabilistic material flow model predicts that a substantial amount of ENMs will be accumulated in stocks, that the magnitude of flows in different regions varies due to differences in population and waste handling and that the concentrations of ENMs in the environment are predicted to be highest in Central Europe and Switzerland.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a dynamic probabilistic material flow and fate model of ENMs, including regional variations in population and waste management systems, in order to estimate flows and concentrations of ENM in the environment.
the development and implementation of dynamic MFA for ENMs in Europe.
the development and application of a dynamic probabilistic model to estimate the flows of ENMs in the EU and in six European sub-regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamic MFA model is a useful tool for assessing the flows of ENMs to the environment and for identifying hotspots of ENM releases.
dynamic MFA can be used to estimate the environmental release and concentration of ENMs in a more realistic manner than static MFA.
the release of ENMs into the environment is highly uncertain and depends on the region and type of ENMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ENMs are released into the environment from nano-products in the EU and in all subregions.
the dynamic model predicts higher environmental concentrations and higher flows of ENMs to the environment than the static model.
dynamic probabilistic MFA models can provide improved predictions of the flows and concentrations of ENM in the environment compared to static MFA models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dynamic probabilistic MFA is a powerful tool to estimate the environmental flows of ENMs and their release concentrations in the environment.
dynamic MFA is a valuable tool to estimate the flows and environmental concentrations of ENMs in the future.
the environmental release of ENMs depends not only on their production volumes but also on the regional characteristics of the countries where they are applied.
